title: What Actually Backs the Value of Money?
question: A dollar isn't backed by gold anymore, and it isn't intrinsically useful the way food or tools are — so what makes it worth anything at all?
summary: Money's value turns out to rest neither on a commodity nor on government decree alone, but on a self-sustaining web of mutual expectation, enforced by taxation and habit — a fiction so stable that most people never notice it's a fiction.
